error_chain: slf4j's LoggerFactory binds at runtime to log4j-slf4j-impl which exposes a Log4jLogger that forwards each call to log4j2's AbstractLogger.logMessage
When the appender chain includes AsyncAppender, log events enter a blocking queue or LMAX Disruptor ring depending on configuration
log4j2's AsyncAppender uses AsyncQueueFullPolicy to decide what to do when the queue is full; the default Discard policy drops events below ERROR level
Under burst load the ring buffer fills, AsyncQueueFullPolicy.Discard drops INFO/DEBUG events silently, and slf4j callers see Logger.info() return without a thrown exception
trigger_conditions: Customer's log4j2 config uses AsyncAppender or AsyncLoggerConfig with the default discard policy
Sustained burst load fills the Disruptor ring beyond ringBufferSize
The discard policy drops sub-ERROR events without error reporting back to slf4j's Logger.info caller

expected_answer.error_origin: log4j2 AsyncQueueFullPolicy.Discard dropping sub-ERROR events when the AsyncAppender ring buffer is full
expected_answer.bypass_reason: slf4j's binding API has no return contract for delivery; log4j2's discard policy silently drops events at the appender rather than back-pressuring callers
expected_answer.correct_config: Set log4j2.AsyncQueueFullPolicy=Default (which blocks the caller) or increase ringBufferSize via AsyncLoggerConfig.RingBufferSize, accepting back-pressure on the slf4j caller path
